scope: Precise MPU faults in the vendored CPU for qemu_flint (PMSAv7), qemu_emery and qemu_gabbro (PMSAv8): synthetic vectors, Rust regression suites, and unchanged 4.37.0 firmware boots
reference: Armv7-M and Armv8-M exception pseudocode (ValidateAddress, PushStack, ExceptionReturn, PreserveFPState) and QEMU's v7m stacking helpers. No native-QEMU capture was made for these vectors.

stackGuardPush.vector: Unprivileged Thread on PSP=0x20001008 executes PUSH {r4-r7}; a 32-byte store-denied guard ends at 0x20001000

before.afterHandlerFirstInstruction: nested MemManage from Handler mode, LR 0xfffffff1

firstFailureBeforeChange.load_multiple_reports_first_denied_addre: MMFAR held the last denied word
firstFailureBeforeChange.unstacking_uses_return_privilege_and_tai: returned to Thread using Handler privilege
firstFailureBeforeChange.lazy_fp_preservation_error_abandons_fp_i: MMFSR 0x82 and FP instruction completed, expected MLSPERR 0x20

syntheticVectors.firstFailingProfile: qemu_flint (each test stops at its first failing profile)

vendoredCoreUnitTests.command: cargo test --release -p rp2350-emu --lib --features test-hooks,testing (standalone copy without the unused tracing-subscriber dev-dependency)
vendoredCoreUnitTests.note: The 21 failures predate this change: absent RP2350 bootrom fixture and upstream expectations superseded by the documented CPS, ITSTATE and MRS corrections. These tests are not part of the parent workspace.

validation.clippy: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes; the vendored library passes with -D warnings
validation.notRun: Browser workflow gate and the compatibility census. npm test and the Wasm build could not be run when these vectors were measured (no npm reachability there); they were run on integration, where the Wasm build and 416 JavaScript/Wasm ABI tests pass with eleven optional fixture skips. Rust dependencies were built from their tagged GitHub sources at the locked versions.
validation.crossCheck: Stacking, unstacking and lazy-preservation behavior compared by reading QEMU target/arm/tcg/m_helper.c and hw/intc/armv7m_nvic.c at f8aef8a (2026-09-18)

integrationRecheck.baselineComparison: The same 20-second boots built from the base commit ecfa7f5 produce identical steps, cycles, frames and FNV digests on all three profiles
integrationRecheck.syntheticVectorsAgainstBase: 12 of 13 fail on ecfa7f5, 13 of 13 pass with this change

firmwareBoot.method: crates/qemu-emery/examples/native_boot.rs, release build, unchanged official 4.37.0 images, fixed epoch, 20 virtual seconds

nativeThroughput.method: The same boot loop built against 80904ec, ecfa7f5 and this change; 8 virtual seconds; three interleaved rounds on one host core; medians of board steps per host second
nativeThroughput.summary: MPU enforcement costs 26% (Emery, Gabbro) and 38% (Flint) of native boot throughput after this change, versus 27% and 42% before it

limits: Synthetic architectural vectors, not native-QEMU or physical-watch captures
Multi-register loads restore all registers on abandonment; the architecture leaves registers loaded before the fault UNKNOWN and QEMU keeps them
An unstacking error leaves r0-r3, r12 and LR unchanged; QEMU keeps the words popped before the error. Both are architecturally permitted

Not modelled: PMSAv8 overlapping-region faults, default-map execute-never regions, unprivileged SCS BusFaults, FPCCR.USER/MMRDY for lazy preservation, a derived HardFault pending behind NMI, precise BusFault and UsageFault abandonment
Host throughput is native, not browser or watch performance
